Carly Fiorina, and the conservative case for feminism

The problem is feminism before it was co-opted had fulfilled its goals. Women can do all that a man can do and get paid the same amount to do it - I can pull out the same study that says $.77 as a Raw Wage Gap and show you when they account for all mitigating factors (seniority, work experience, hours worked, negotiation, and education) that women make the same amount as men and more than men in many categories and job fields. There just isn't much that is left. Women can even fill combat roles in the military if they can complete the same physical tests; this should be a given because of how much on at stake with physical fitness in combat units.

The worst thing that can possibly happen to a movement is to achieve its goals.

You're left with a whole organisational power structure and nothing to do with it. You have to make up a new goal to start working towards.

Now, if you're the March of Dimes and your goal was to cure polio, and you cure polio, that's not such a disaster, because there's always another disease you can fight.

But if the goal of your movement was "equality", and you achieve equality, you've got nowhere else to go except to start fighting for supremacy.
